• Youth Employment and Skills Strategy (YESS)

    Canada Summer Jobs

    Canada Summer Jobs (CSJ) is a program under the Youth Employment and Skills Strategy (YESS). It helps youth aged 15 to 30 gain paid summer work experience and develop skills for the job market.

    Not-for-profit employers can receive funding for up to 100% of the provincial or territorial minimum wage and public and private sector employers are eligible to receive funding for up to 50%

    Red Seal Completion Bonus

    The Red Seal Completion Bonus (the Bonus) is a $5,000 payment for eligible journeypersons who complete an apprenticeship training program and receive certification in a designated Red Seal trade.

    $5,000 per designated Red Seal trade in which you complete an apprenticeship and receive certification.

    Union Training and Innovation Program – Infrastructure Expansion

    This funding opportunity aims to strengthen Canada’s skilled trades workforce by expanding training capacity and modernizing union-led training infrastructure to increase training spaces. It will fund projects that upgrade training facilities, expand capacity, and invest in new infrastructure through renovations, expansions and construction of new training facilities.

  • Social Development Partnerships Program (SDPP-D)

    Accessible Canada – National AccessAbility Week Funding – 2025 and 2026

    This funding opportunity aims to support projects that increase awareness through National Accessibility Week (NAAW) activities in 2025 and in 2026. It will fund projects that improve understanding and knowledge of Canadians on accessibility and disability inclusion, reduce stigma and attitudinal barriers towards persons with disabilities, and share best practices and lessons learned related to NAAW activities within the disability community.

    Up to $100,000 or $200,000 (with special requirements) for a project that is up to 2 years

  • Social Development Partnership Program

    Social Development Partnership Program - Disability Component - Disability Benefits Navigation

    The Disability Benefits Navigation program will help to facilitate greater access to disability benefits for persons with disabilities and their families, including the Disability Tax Credit (DTC), the Canada Disability Benefit (CDB), as well as other federal, provincial and territorial disability benefits. Disability Benefits Navigation (DBN) targets individuals who may be eligible for disability benefits yet remain underserved, disconnected from services, or face intersecting barriers to access.

    Up to $1,000,000 (up to $500,000 per year) for a project that is 2 years in duration

    • Not accepting applications
    • Social Development and Community Building

    Social Development Partnerships Program – Disability Component - Disability Benefits Navigation (Navigation Services)

    The Social Development Partnerships Program - Disability Component (SDPP-D) is a grants and contributions program that seeks to improve the participation and social inclusion of persons with disabilities in all aspects of Canadian society. The Disability Support Navigation call for proposals under this program focuses on helping people with disabilities and their families access disability programs and benefits.
